title: Re: Nimbleware pilot — cost sensitivity & latency tiers
text:
Re: Nimbleware pilot — cost sensitivity & latency tiers

["From: Mara Chen <mara@nimbleware.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbleware.com
Date: 2027-09-29T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Nimbleware pilot — initial numbers and follow-up

Hey Logan,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — the team liked the consistency and the console walkthrough. I promised to share a quick summary of the numbers we discussed and confirm a few asks so we can land a pilot+SOW. Below are the initial estimates from our side: 

- Active users (starting month): 35k MAU
- Average prompts per user/day: 5 (mix of short chat & structured generation)
- Estimated tokens per prompt (avg): 300 tokens
- Forecasted monthly token volume (1st 30 days): ~157.5M tokens
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent requests

Primary asks for qualification:
1) Target blended cost: we need to be in the $8k–$18k/mo range initially, which equates to roughly $50–$115 per 1M tokens for our projected volume (we know these ranges are broad).
2) Latency SLO: target 200ms p95 for the core inline chat experience — acceptable to have a higher-cost path for 20% of traffic.
3) Pilot length: 6 weeks technical + 6 weeks evaluation.

Can you confirm which tier routing and batching approach would meet the 200ms p95 for the core experience and what incremental cost we'd expect for the 20% low-latency route? Also attaching the token profile and MAU estimates.

Thanks,
Mara
Mara Chen
Head of Product, Nimbleware

Attachments: nimbleware_token_profile.csv, nimbleware_mau_estimates.xlsx", 'From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Mara Chen <mara@nimbleware.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-29T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbleware pilot — initial numbers and follow-up

Hi Mara — really appreciate the clear numbers and the timeline. Quick read and next steps below.

Summary of what those volumes imply (ballpark):
- ~157.5M tok/mo = ~5.25M tokens/day
- With continuous traffic and 120 concurrency, we recommend a split routing pilot:
  * Low-latency route (streaming, premium SLO): ~20% traffic — optimized for <200ms p95 — expect higher unit cost due to smaller batch sizes and reserved capacity to avoid queueing.
  * Cost-optimized route (batching + smart prefix caching): ~80% traffic — relax p95 to ~400–600ms depending on load — large batching drives unit costs down significantly.

High-level cost guidance for pilot (monthly):
- Streaming (20% of traffic, 31.5M tok/mo): target unit $/1M tokens ~ $70–$95 => incremental cost ~ $2,205 – $2,992
- Batching (80% of traffic, 126M tok/mo): target unit $/1M tokens ~ $10–$18 => incremental cost ~ $1,260 – $2,268
- Total estimated band (pilot profile): $3,465 – $5,260/mo (this does not include one-time setup/ingress or dedicated SLA fees)

Notes: these are conservative pilot estimates — if you can accept slightly larger latency on the 80% route (700–900ms), the batching unit can drop further to sub-$8/1M. Conversely, tighter p95 on the streaming route (e.g., <120ms) will push the streaming unit to $120–$160/1M.

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll prepare a short pricing proposal with two route configs (attached as redwood_pricing_proposal_v1.pdf).
2) Monica to run a quick infrastructure check for concurrency and recommend reserved capacity for the 20% streaming slice.
3) Schedule a technical sync (30–45m) with your infra and product leads — suggested window: Thu 09/30 10:00–11:00 PT.

Action items for you: confirm acceptance of the 20/80 split for the pilot and confirm the DocuSign process for the SOW.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

', "From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbleware pilot — cost sensitivity & routing proposal

Hi Mara — adding a couple of operational details from our side that affect cost and the SLO guarantees: 

1) Reserved vs burst capacity: for predictable <200ms p95 we recommend reserving a small pool of GPUs for the streaming slice. For your stated peak, reserving ~2–3 GPUs in the pilot region should keep p95 under 200ms with some headroom; cost is mostly the reserved capacity and the streaming unit premium.
2) Batching strategy: we can enable adaptive batching with a max batching window of 30–50ms to keep the 80% path responsive while still harvesting batching efficiency. That approach typically halves the per-token cost vs naive single-request execution.
3) Quality/regression checks: we’ll instrument a prompt-level quality monitor tied to the evaluation set you shared; if model quality drops when we switch quantization or more aggressive batching, we’ll automatically route mismatch traffic to the higher-cost path.

I'll coordinate with our provisioning team after Logan confirms the pilot split. I attached the draft proposal (redwood_pricing_proposal_v1.pdf) — it includes explicit unit bands, reserved-capacity line items, and a pilot SLA for infra uptime.

Thanks — Monica
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-09-30T11:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Nimbleware pilot — cost sensitivity & routing proposal

Thanks Logan/Monica — this is helpful and lines up with what our CFO expected. Quick confirmations from our side: 

- We accept the proposed 20/80 split for the pilot.
- Nimbleware legal will review the SOW; please route the DocuSign to legal@nimbleware.com and procurement@nimbleware.com.
- We’d like the pilot to include a month-over-month report: token burn, p95 latency, routing percentages, and cost-to-date.

One last ask: could you provide an alternate quote that targets $30/1M tokens blended (aggressive) so we can show two scenarios to finance? If that is unrealistic for our volume profile, please state the main levers we can pull (larger batching window, accept higher p95 on the cost route, or commit to a higher reserved capacity monthly commit).

I’ll confirm SOW routing once legal returns.

Best,
Mara
